choices.B: Providers must recall and permanently decommission any high-risk AI system that receives more than five user complaints about output quality within any twelve-month monitoring period
choices.C: Providers must establish and document a post-market monitoring system proportionate to the nature of the AI system, collecting and analysing performance data to identify changes in data quality that may affect compliance
choices.D: Providers must submit all system outputs to the national market surveillance authority in real time so that the authority can independently assess data quality on a continuous basis

explanation: Article 72 of the AI Act requires providers of high-risk AI systems to establish and document a post-market monitoring system in a manner proportionate to the nature of the technologies and risks, systematically collecting, documenting and analysing relevant data on performance throughout the system's lifetime.

question: Under the GDPR (EU) 2016/679, what is the maximum timeframe within which a data controller must notify the supervisory authority of a personal data breach?

choices.A: Without undue delay and, where feasible, not later than 72 hours after having become aware of the personal data breach
choices.B: Within 30 calendar days of discovering the breach, after completing a comprehensive internal investigation and impact assessment
choices.C: Within 7 working days of the breach, provided the breach is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons
choices.D: Within 24 hours of the breach occurring, regardless of whether the controller has yet become aware that a breach has taken place

explanation: Article 33(1) of the GDPR requires the controller to notify the competent supervisory authority of a personal data breach without undue delay and, where feasible, not later than 72 hours after having become aware of it.

question: Under the GDPR (EU) 2016/679, what does the principle of 'integrity and confidentiality' require of data controllers?

choices.A: Personal data must be accessible only to the data subject themselves and may not be viewed or processed by any employee of the data controller under any circumstances
choices.B: Personal data must be processed in a manner that ensures appropriate security, including protection against unauthorised processing and accidental loss, using appropriate technical and organisational measures
choices.C: Personal data must be stored exclusively in encrypted databases located within the physical territory of the European Union and may never be transmitted over public networks
choices.D: Personal data must be printed on tamper-proof paper and stored in fireproof vaults, since the GDPR does not recognise digital storage as meeting the integrity requirement

explanation: Article 5(1)(f) of the GDPR establishes the integrity and confidentiality principle, requiring that personal data be processed in a manner that ensures appropriate security, including protection against unauthorised or unlawful processing and against accidental loss, destruction or damage, using appropriate technical or organisational measures.

question: Under the GDPR (EU) 2016/679, when is a data controller required to carry out a Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA)?

choices.A: Only when the data controller plans to transfer personal data to a third country that has not received an adequacy decision from the European Commission under Article 45
choices.B: When a type of processing, in particular using new technologies, is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons, considering the nature, scope, context and purposes
choices.C: Before processing any personal data whatsoever, regardless of the nature, scope or likelihood of risk, as a mandatory prerequisite for all data processing activities across the EU
choices.D: Exclusively when a supervisory authority issues a formal written order requiring the controller to conduct an assessment for a specific processing activity already underway

explanation: Article 35(1) of the GDPR requires a DPIA where a type of processing, in particular using new technologies and taking into account the nature, scope, context and purposes of processing, is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons.

question: Under Regulation (EU) 2018/1725 on data protection for EU institutions, what are the conditions under which an EU institution may transfer personal data to a third country?

choices.A: Transfers to third countries are categorically prohibited regardless of any safeguards, since EU institutions may only process personal data within EU territory exclusively
choices.B: Transfers may occur on the basis of an adequacy decision by the Commission, appropriate safeguards such as standard contractual clauses, or specific derogations for limited situations
choices.C: Transfers are permitted only to countries that are members of the Council of Europe and have ratified Convention 108 on data protection, with no other basis available
choices.D: Transfers may occur freely to any third country provided the data subject is informed within thirty calendar days after the transfer has already taken place

explanation: Chapter V of Regulation (EU) 2018/1725 establishes the framework for international transfers, allowing transfers based on an adequacy decision (Article 47), appropriate safeguards including standard contractual clauses (Article 48), or specific derogations for limited situations (Article 50).

question: Under the AI Act (EU) 2024/1689, certain AI practices are entirely prohibited. Which of the following is classified as a prohibited AI practice?

choices.A: AI systems that perform weather forecasting using satellite imagery and historical meteorological data to generate public alerts about severe weather events
choices.B: AI systems that assist medical professionals by analysing diagnostic imaging to detect early signs of disease, provided the final diagnosis is confirmed by a qualified human doctor
choices.C: AI systems that provide automated translation services between official EU languages for use in internal communications between EU institutions and Member State administrations
choices.D: AI systems that deploy subliminal techniques or purposefully manipulative or deceptive techniques to materially distort behaviour, causing significant harm to the person or others

explanation: Article 5(1)(a) of the AI Act prohibits AI systems that deploy subliminal techniques beyond a person's consciousness, or purposefully manipulative or deceptive techniques, with the objective or effect of materially distorting the behaviour of a person or group in a manner that causes or is reasonably likely to cause significant harm.

question: Under the GDPR (EU) 2016/679, what is the maximum administrative fine that can be imposed for the most serious infringements, such as violations of the basic principles for processing or data subjects' rights?

choices.A: Up to EUR 10 million, or in the case of an undertaking, up to 2% of total worldwide annual turnover of the preceding financial year, whichever is higher
choices.B: Up to EUR 5 million per individual data subject affected by the infringement, with the total fine uncapped and calculated based on the number of affected persons
choices.C: Up to EUR 50 million with no alternative calculation based on annual turnover, applicable equally to all data controllers regardless of their size or revenue
choices.D: Up to EUR 20 million, or in the case of an undertaking, up to 4% of total worldwide annual turnover of the preceding financial year, whichever is higher

explanation: Article 83(5) of the GDPR provides that infringements of the basic principles for processing (Article 5), data subjects' rights (Articles 12-22), or international transfer provisions shall be subject to administrative fines up to EUR 20 million, or in the case of an undertaking, up to 4% of total worldwide annual turnover of the preceding financial year, whichever is higher.

question: Under the AI Act (EU) 2024/1689, what is the definition of an 'AI system'?

choices.A: Any software application that processes structured data using predefined business rules and deterministic logic without any capability for machine learning or inference
choices.B: A machine-based system designed to operate with varying levels of autonomy, that may exhibit adaptiveness and that infers, from input, how to generate outputs such as predictions, content, recommendations, or decisions
choices.C: A hardware device equipped with sensors that collects environmental data and transmits it to a central server for manual analysis by human operators without any automated processing
choices.D: A digital tool that exclusively performs statistical calculations on historical datasets and produces fixed reports without generating predictions or adaptive recommendations

explanation: Article 3(1) of the AI Act defines an 'AI system' as a machine-based system that is designed to operate with varying levels of autonomy, that may exhibit adaptiveness after deployment, and that, for explicit or implicit objectives, infers, from the input it receives, how to generate outputs such as predictions, content, recommendations, or decisions that can influence physical or virtual environments.

question: Under the AI Act (EU) 2024/1689, the risk-based classification system categorises AI systems into four risk levels. Which level subjects the AI system to the most stringent requirements before market placement?

choices.A: High-risk AI systems, which must comply with requirements on data quality, documentation, transparency, human oversight, accuracy, robustness, and cybersecurity before being placed on the market
choices.B: Unacceptable-risk AI systems, which may be placed on the market after paying a special levy to the national market surveillance authority that funds ongoing monitoring activities
choices.C: Limited-risk AI systems, which require prior authorisation from the European Artificial Intelligence Board and annual renewal of their compliance certificates to remain operational
choices.D: Minimal-risk AI systems, which must undergo a full conformity assessment conducted by an independent notified body before they can be marketed anywhere in the European Union

explanation: The AI Act establishes four risk levels: unacceptable (prohibited), high (subject to strict requirements in Articles 8-15 before market placement), limited (transparency obligations), and minimal (no specific obligations). Unacceptable risk systems are banned outright, so high-risk is the category with the most stringent compliance requirements for systems that may be placed on the market.

question: Under the AI Act (EU) 2024/1689, what specific obligations apply to providers of general-purpose AI (GPAI) models regarding transparency?

choices.A: Providers must obtain individual consent from every person whose data was used in training the model and publish a searchable registry of all training data sources on their website
choices.B: Providers must disclose the complete source code of their GPAI models on a publicly accessible open-source repository approved by the European AI Office within thirty days of release
choices.C: Providers must submit their GPAI models for mandatory pre-market testing by the European Artificial Intelligence Board, which issues a public certification grade for each model version
choices.D: Providers must draw up and keep up to date technical documentation, provide information and documentation to downstream providers integrating the model, establish a copyright compliance policy, and publish a training content summary

explanation: Article 53 of the AI Act requires providers of GPAI models to draw up and maintain technical documentation, provide information and documentation to downstream providers, put in place a policy to comply with Union copyright law, and make publicly available a sufficiently detailed summary about the content used for training.

question: Under the AI Act (EU) 2024/1689, deployers of high-risk AI systems in the workplace have specific obligations. What must they do before putting such a system into use?

choices.A: Deployers must inform workers' representatives and affected workers that they will be subject to the use of the high-risk AI system, providing transparency about its deployment
choices.B: Deployers must obtain unanimous written consent from every individual employee who will be affected by the AI system before the system can be activated in the workplace
choices.C: Deployers must replace all existing human decision-making processes with the high-risk AI system within ninety days of receiving the CE marking certificate for the system
choices.D: Deployers must hire a certified AI auditor to permanently monitor every decision produced by the AI system and manually override any output that deviates from historical patterns

explanation: Article 26(7) of the AI Act requires deployers using high-risk AI systems in the workplace to inform workers' representatives and the affected workers that they will be subject to the use of the high-risk AI system, prior to putting it into use.

question: Under the AI Act (EU) 2024/1689, GPAI models classified as having 'systemic risk' face additional obligations. What is the threshold for this classification, and what extra requirements apply?

choices.A: A GPAI model has systemic risk if it has more than one million registered users in the EU; additional obligations include real-time output monitoring by the European AI Office and mandatory weekly compliance reports
choices.B: A GPAI model is classified as systemic risk if it is deployed by any EU institution; additional obligations include mandatory open-source licensing and publication of all model weights on a Commission-hosted repository
choices.C: A GPAI model has systemic risk if its provider's annual revenue exceeds EUR 500 million; additional obligations include paying a systemic risk levy and maintaining a permanent liaison officer at the European AI Office
choices.D: A GPAI model is presumed to have systemic risk if its cumulative training compute exceeds 10^25 FLOPs; additional obligations include model evaluation, adversarial testing, incident tracking, and ensuring adequate cybersecurity protection

explanation: Article 51 of the AI Act presumes systemic risk when the cumulative amount of compute used for training exceeds 10^25 floating point operations. Article 55 imposes additional obligations including performing model evaluations, assessing and mitigating systemic risks, tracking and reporting serious incidents, and ensuring adequate cybersecurity protection.

question: Under the AI Act (EU) 2024/1689, what governance body is established at EU level to oversee AI regulation, and what are its primary functions?

choices.A: The European Data Innovation Board, which is repurposed exclusively for AI governance and stripped of all previous advisory functions related to data sharing and data spaces
choices.B: The European AI Enforcement Agency, an independent agency with the power to directly impose fines on AI providers and to suspend the operation of any AI system within the single market
choices.C: The European Artificial Intelligence Board (the 'AI Board'), composed of Member State representatives, which advises on consistent application, facilitates cooperation, and provides guidance on implementation of the AI Act
choices.D: The European AI Court, a judicial body with exclusive jurisdiction over all disputes arising from the deployment of AI systems within the EU, replacing national courts in these matters

explanation: Article 65 of the AI Act establishes the European Artificial Intelligence Board, composed of one representative from each Member State, which advises and assists the Commission and Member States in facilitating the consistent and effective application of the regulation across the EU.
